Where it began

Mohammad Younis Khan was born in Mardan on 29 November 1977. He came into the Pakistan side when Sri Lanka toured in early 2000, making his Test debut on 26 February.

The early years were stop-start. The turning point was October 2004, when he was given the number three spot against Sri Lanka in Karachi. He made it his own.

The player

Younis played 118 Tests between 2000 and 2017 and made 10,099 runs at 52.06, with 34 hundreds and 33 fifties. In April 2017 he became the first Pakistani to reach 10,000 Test runs, and by the time he retired that year no one from Pakistan had made more Test runs or more Test hundreds.

There was 267 at Bangalore on the 2005 tour of India, which set up the win that levelled the series. There was 313 against Sri Lanka at Karachi in February 2009, in his first Test as captain, which saved the match and took him to the top of the ICC Test batting rankings. And there was 171 not out at Pallekele in July 2015, as Pakistan chased 377 to win. It was his fifth fourth-innings Test hundred, a first in the game.

What made him special

He was rated among the best players of spin bowling anywhere, and he loved the leg side, with the flick as his favourite stroke. He could be flamboyant, going down on one knee to drive, but there was a hard core of grit beneath it. When he retired he was the only Test cricketer to have made a hundred in all 11 countries that had hosted Test matches. In the field he was the first Pakistani to hold 100 Test catches, and he finished with 139.

The flick had its price. Early in an innings it got him out leg before more often than he would have liked, and every so often he left a ball that was heading for the stumps. His leg-spin was very occasional, nine Test wickets at 54.56, and Craig McMillan once took 26 off one of his overs in Hamilton.

Away from the middle

At the Rose Bowl in 2007, playing for Yorkshire against Hampshire, he made 106 and 202 not out, the first Yorkshire player to score a hundred and a double hundred in the same match.

In 2009 he captained Pakistan to their first World Twenty20 title, beating Sri Lanka at Lord's. Pakistan gave him the Pride of Performance in 2010 and the Sitara-i-Imtiaz in 2018, and he was a Wisden Cricketer of the Year. After retiring he passed on what he knew, including a spell as Pakistan's batting coach in 2020. Given a free day, he liked to go fishing.

And finally

Younis and Misbah-ul-Haq left Test cricket together after the 2017 tour of the West Indies. Their last match, at Roseau in May, ended in a 101-run win and a 2–1 series victory. When they left, no Pakistan pair had added more runs together in Tests. It is hard to think of better company to walk off with.
